invariants.name: drift_recovery_known_transforms
invariants.invariant: representation equivalence: a transient generated by a known (frequency, phase) transformation of the reference must be restored to the reference, and the estimated drift must match the known transformation modulo the spectral-width and cycle aliases
invariants.rationale: New 768-point/2400 Hz/f0=127.7 dataset with four known drifts (8.9 to 31.2 Hz, both signs) registered with the API-default (0,0) hint. Pre-fix, the local least-squares optimizer seeded from (0,0) stalls in wrong local minima for 2 of 4 transients (estimates off by ~63 Hz, corrected signals ~94% mismatched), so the max-error assertions fail. Post-fix, the global scan plus windowed polish recovers all four drifts to sub-Hz accuracy and the corrected transients match the reference, so all assertions pass.

invariants.name: drift_hint_invariance
invariants.invariant: symmetry/invariance: the registration result is a property of the data, so wildly different drift hints ((0,0), (37.4,0.55), (-41.2,-0.31)) must yield the same corrected transients and (aliased) drift estimates, and the no-hint result must be correct
invariants.rationale: Pre-fix, each initial_guess is the only starting point of a local optimization, so different hints land in different basins: the pairwise relative differences of the corrected stacks reach ~0.94, failing the 0.01 invariance bound (and the (0,0)-hint result itself is wrong for 2 transients). Post-fix, the coarse global scan makes every start converge to the same global alignment, so all pairwise differences are ~0 and the assertion passes.

invariants.name: windowed_registration_stable_region
invariants.invariant: spatial (spectral-window) invariance: drift must be estimated from the stable registration window only; a transient carrying a strong extra spectral component outside that window (here a 2x-amplitude peak at +260 Hz) must still be aligned by the windowed registration, and the stable window of the corrected transient must match the reference
invariants.rationale: Pre-fix, the documented tuple frequency_range API is broken: the weight-mask expression 'lo < axis & axis < hi' parses as 'lo < (axis & axis) < hi' and raises TypeError (bitwise_and on floats) the moment spectral_registration is called with a window, so the test fails immediately; even the workflow path ignores the window. Post-fix, the windowed comparison works: the direct API and the workflow both return the true (-21.3 Hz, 0.42) drift (errors 0.27 Hz / 0.008 cycles) and the windowed residual of the corrected transient is 0.048, well under the 0.2 limit.

invariants.name: unusable_transient_rejection
invariants.invariant: quality-control conservation: unusable transients must be flagged so they cannot pollute the reported average; with reject_threshold=0.5 a drift+noise transient is accepted (small residual) while a pure-noise transient is rejected (large best-achievable residual)
invariants.rationale: Pre-fix, register_dynamic_series hard-codes accepted=True for every transient and ignores reject_threshold, so the noise transient is accepted (observed accepted=[True, True]) and the assertion 'noise-only transient was accepted' fails. Post-fix, the windowed after-residuals are ~0.004 (good) and ~0.88 (noise), giving accepted=[True, False] and passing all four assertions.

invariants.name: averaging_snr_improvement
invariants.invariant: the scientific goal of the repair: registering drifted MRS transients before averaging must improve the averaged spectrum - averaged SNR must rise by at least the averaging gain and the windowed residual ratio must collapse relative to the unregistered series
invariants.rationale: New 8-transient series with independent drifts of 17-33 Hz (both signs), random phases and 3% noise. Pre-fix, most transients are misaligned (the (0,0)-seeded local optimizer stalls), so the average stays smeared: SNR only 15.4 -> 31.0 (2.01x < required 3.5x) and windowed residual 1.381 -> 0.942 (0.68x > allowed 0.2x), both assertions fail. Post-fix, all transients align and averaging sharpens the peaks: SNR 15.4 -> 62.3 (4.04x) and windowed residual 1.381 -> 0.228 (0.17x), both assertions pass.

notes: All five tests were executed against a full pre-fix checkout (git HEAD version of source/suspect/processing/frequency_correction.py) and against the patched tree: each FAILs pre-fix (AssertionError, or TypeError from the broken tuple frequency_range mask for test 3) and PASSes post-fix with the margins quoted in the rationales. All inputs are synthetic (own n, dt, f0, peak positions, windows, drifts, seeds); the public fixture and its values are not used. Not tested: private verification magnitudes; also, the post-fix local polish uses a soft maxfev stop, so on narrow-peak landscapes it can settle ~1 Hz off the optimum - tolerances (2 Hz / 0.2 windowed residual) are set comfortably above that observed behaviour, and test 3 deliberately uses a landscape where the true drift is the unique windowed global minimum so any correct implementation passes.
